record_notes.DCP-LETT-1851: April 8, supplied 1856, nine surviving blocks. Lindley medal advocacy and Council politics answer a missing Hooker communication, not the older packet contexts. Falconer address is conditional. P5 introduces Charles’s reply to Mrs Hooker’s note to Emma, followed by visit logistics in Charles’s voice. P6 has genuine MathML nine and one-half miles, not 912. Croydon carriage and Huxley visit are prospective; later medal outcome and railway completion are apparatus, not contemporary knowledge. Full metadata, exclusions, footnotes and bibliography read.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1869: May 7, 1856 incomplete Hooker memorandum, all 21 surviving blocks, annotations, notes and bibliography read. Nymphaea seeds available in autumn, not dispatched. Ascension native flora and fern distinction, Hedyotis correction and wind/garden hypotheses are qualified. Albumen constancy is contrasted with species variation; Bentham observed rather than cultivated Montpellier dandelions. Glyceria wild food differs from Zizania cultivation. Drège table loan offered, not received; raw diag/ramme strings damage list formatting. Primrose/cowslip ranges, Royal Society map delivery, lost Lyallia comparison, Herefordshire intermediates and Targioni/Candolle discussion remain distinct. P21 explicitly asks about Overstone, Huxley and Athenaeum support through Strzelecki: worker summary wrongly says committee questions absent. Separate Darwin notes and later May 13 Lyallia use are not the initial receipt. Distinctive P21 supports 1870 P2; botanical/map portions support 1874 P1–2.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1870: May 9, supplied 1856, seven blocks and full apparatus. P1 forwards Crowe material and asks for advice; a similar earlier Crowe letter is not assumed to be this enclosure. P2 answers 1869 P21 on Huxley candidature, named committee intermediaries, Owen’s likely opposition and risk of rejection. P3–5 develop Lyell’s oral publication advice and Darwin’s objection to a thin sketch without references; not a reply to Hooker’s botanical memorandum. Emma received Mrs Hooker’s note that morning, a separate receipt owner. Only P2 is accepted as the demonstrated response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1874: May 11, supplied 1856, ten blocks and complete apparatus. P1 explicitly thanks two long letters; first is May 7 memorandum, second missing response to May 9. Botanical facts and Drège acknowledge 1869; Forbes map is to be collected in London, not yet in Darwin’s custody. P1 additionally reports Council news and anticipated Richardson medal; Treasury approval May 22 and November award are later. Crowe/Huxley/publication discussion primarily answers missing second letter. P9 concerns Mrs Hooker and Gosse; P10 reopens preliminary-sketch anxiety. Preserve partial response P1–2 and do not synthesize the second incoming letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1876: May 21, supplied 1856, five blocks, notes and bibliography read. Darwin has received and read Huxley’s first two published lectures, regards tone as too vehement, and pauses Athenaeum action. Letter to Huxley and Hooker’s intervening input are missing. Generalisation about quarrelling anatomists has stated exceptions. Plant-range and fossil Casuarina/Banksia inquiries are new requests; Fucus paper loan requested, not already received. No preserved distinctive incoming prompt established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1885: June 1, supplied 1856, seven blocks, exclusions, notes and bibliography. Hooker’s unutterable mortification concerns germination/dispersal, not a wrong printed assertion as editorial summary suggests. Darwin jokes about Kew closure before understanding the note; argues Hooker’s rejection of multiple creations favours dispersal evidence. Seed credit to Consul Hunt and partly illegible sender is qualified, with earlier Hunt letter only provenance lead. Old Red Sandstone leaf report, Sharpe’s death heard May 31, fireworks fatigue and desired Candolle review are distinct. Review is requested, not read. Current Hooker prompt missing.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1904: June 17–18, supplied 1856, eight blocks and full apparatus. Main text answers a missing Hooker note received June 17, weighing Huxley/Falconer/Cuvier and qualified morphological inference, with Wollaston book already read and separate missing Wollaston remark. Woodward continental-island report prompted June 16 letter to Lyell, but precise Woodward source is not fixed merely by similar subject. P7 explicitly dated 18th establishes Lyell June 17 letter known by June 18, not by June 17. P8 second postscript asks North-West American plant question and should retain its section/date context. Unidentified hand corrected ludged to lugged; no authorial correction silently inferred.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1908: June 22, supplied 1856, five blocks and complete apparatus. P1 cites Flora and Gärtner Laburnum abstracts actually seen, not necessarily whole works. P2–3 narrow earlier North-West American plant request to plants absent from Siberia or continental America, with an approximate count explicitly acceptable. P4 Mrs Hooker’s ticket received June 22 and Emma’s pregnancy health are separate. 1911 P1 and P5 directly answer the distribution and Flora discussion; this is a reverse reply, not Darwin target prose.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1911: Incomplete Hooker note, six surviving blocks and full scholarly apparatus. Original XML explicitly has mutually exclusive June 26 OR July 3, 1856, not a continuous interval. P1 rejects proposed NW American examples because of Altai/Baikal/Dahuria occurrences, retains western endemics, and plans an Asa Gray inquiry. P2 distinguishes transport survival from establishment using different Asiatic and Azorean Entada seedlings. P3 reports premature pollen shedding; Viscum observation is later corrected, not silently repaired now. P4 asks about Radlkofer/Siebold parthenogenesis. P5 proposes Flora translation and a translations-only Ray Society. P6 reports Thomson’s Aldrovanda rediscovery; terminal words absolutely identical with S. European local plants were added by Darwin, presumably copied from the missing ending, not a secure Hooker-autograph segment. Separate Darwin annotations are undated. Source-specific response appears in 1919 P4–10, known by July 5; reverse response to 1908 in P1/P5.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1918: Morning July 5, supplied 1856, four blocks and complete apparatus. Brief thanks for interesting note before post closes; substantive new request to re-examine marked Tristan list and Fuegian/circumpolar relations. Actual list and red crosses are unavailable here. No Lyell route occurs in the body; editorial summary belongs to evening 1919. Generic thanks alone does not justify a separate fully scoped training reply. Morning precedes 1919 by its explicit internal reference.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1919: Evening July 5, supplied 1856, all thirteen blocks, notes and bibliography. P1 develops Tristan/Antarctic-continent question from morning letter. P2 acknowledges Lyell long reply, P3 requests forwarding of Darwin’s letter, which is not yet established as done. P4–10 directly answer 1911: Flora/Laburnum translation and follow-up, Entada establishment, Aristolochia/Viscum and stigma readiness, parthenogenesis, Aldrovanda with remembered Candolle parallel, and Ray Society policy based on own Cirripedia experience. P11 £20 is pledge, not February 1857 recorded payment. P13 asks for intermediate-variety examples after Wollaston; other subject and missing prior cases. Editorial summary belongs to morning 1918. Receipt of Hooker note some days ago is relative, not an exact date. Lyell source is a journal extract of missing original, so known-by acknowledgement does not prove every retained diagram or unsent postscript was received.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1921: July 8, supplied 1856, six blocks and complete apparatus. Darwin discovers previously scored Tristan passage he had forgotten and partly withdraws request; this is rereading, not first receipt. Chile–New Zealand subset copied from Hooker list, with habitat/range questions; full underlying and copied lists not transcribed. P5 began rereading Galápagos paper last night, July 7, not a completed reread. Lyell verdict still unclear. No distinctive surviving current Hooker input established for a direct pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1889: Additional Woodward source June 4, 1856, nine blocks, annotations, notes and bibliography. Sharpe bereavement, credits to Waterhouse/Forbes/Hooker and request for written Darwin memoranda after May 27 discussion. Waterhouse agrees old island-fauna theory; Tasmanian sequence and migration claims differ from universal all-island continental assertion. South American islands hypothesised submerged/recolonised since older Tertiary. Whewell discussion and Pickering human-race claims attributed, not Darwin voice. Monster map and larger exposition hoped within six years, awaiting Darwin species work. Could inform 1904 P3, but main evidence does not uniquely identify this particular note over other Woodward communication; keep candidate without accepted knowledge date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1807: Additional Woodward memorandum after June 4, 1856, nine blocks, separate Darwin annotations, three footnotes and bibliography. Lists representative shell species with qualified identities across Europe, Greenland and North America, supplementing answers on another Darwin manuscript. Page references are to Manual of Mollusca; broader north-Atlantic land-way claim is quoted in editorial explanation of the book, not itself complete letter prose. Darwin annotation records having the note, but is undated. This does not resolve exact source of June 17 continental-island paraphrase. Preserve June 5–30 XML bounds and after-date qualification.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1905: Additional Lyell June 17, 1856 copy, ten blocks and complete apparatus. Challenges continental-area reasoning through Sharpe’s proposed glacial submergence, elapsed geological time and Darwin’s coral subsidence. Lyell qualifies post-Eocene geographical change rather than licensing all arbitrary land bridges. Haughton’s eleven-mile sounding is doubted, not established fact. New Zealand earthquake/tree age is analogy; Madeira/Porto Santo biological contrast remains question. Chatham/Raoul identification has editorial uncertainty. Darwin’s explicitly June 18 Hooker postscript acknowledges this side of the argument; known-by June 18, no exact receipt hour or final-copy wording guarantee.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1915A: Additional Lyell contemporary journal extract headed July 1, 1856, fifteen blocks, full notes/bibliography and all three actual figures read. Original sent letter missing; copy/extract is not proof of full dispatch extent. Volcanic elevation versus broad ocean subsidence debated with qualified mechanism, not a settled universal law. Source 12,000-foot sounding conflicts with apparatus 1,200; preserve discrepancy. P9 genuine MathML means one-half million years, not 12 million. First journal diagram is reportedly dated June 1 against July 1 heading, an unresolved layer. Drawings show hypothetical sea levels/volcano/deformed layers, littoral flanking beds and Grand Canary overlap; no measured scale. July 2 postscript in footnote 8 is expressly NOT sent to Darwin and cannot be incoming memory. 1919 P2 acknowledges main Lyell answer by July 5, while extent of copy/diagrams received remains limited.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1774: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 8 with supplied month/year. P1 unidentified seed returned by Hooker is distinct from P9 note giving names of the two Norwegian seeds. Darwin only presumes the returned seed dead or not worth planting; not verified viability. Requests Miquel loan to recalculate Candolle and asks Boreau size. Postscript explicitly says identification note just received, allowing November 8 receipt event for that missing note without inventing its body. Reports nine pigeon varieties and reluctance to kill them. Indian Flora scheme and self-revision of Decaisne objection reflect additional missing correspondence. Later 1870 revival is editorial future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1781: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 14, supplied 1855. Thanks missing information on requested books, makes purchase conditional on price. Believes reported old raspberry seeds but distinguishes sixty from two thousand years and is uncertain about chemical change. Rejects Bentham proposed soil search as difficult and inconclusive, not as a failed performed experiment. Asks whether plants become social after introduction and proposes conditional explanatory value of such cases; later notes saying Hooker and Bentham say yes cannot be projected into this question. Penultimate missing Hooker note reported improved baby; Wollaston return with almost eleven thousand insects is reported news. 1774 is an outgoing enquiry, not this reply input.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1785: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Conjectured November 23, 1855, original Friday morning. A possible Lindley invitation is conditional on health, council duties, time and social familiarity. Darwin would like to go but anticipates possible inability; later nonattendance at council is not already a fact. Differences over charlock evidence are explicitly personal scientific disagreement, not acceptance of Hooker view. Missing invitation/discussion note prevents a direct pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1736: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 9 with supplied month/year despite low document number. Responds to Hooker published December 8 report, which praised charlock evidence while retaining moisture-resistance doubts, and to Loranthus deception example. Only excerpts of that publication occur in apparatus, not full original incoming source. Proposes seed burial in a public garden for long-term records, alternatively his own plot at nine inches with brick sides; experiment is not already begun. Ten-year horizon and stated future age are source prose, not a new exact dateline. Seemann memorandum is unlocated; meeting discussion prospective.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Two schematic panels: A/B/C terrain with F volcano, B–D and G relative sea levels and deep K–L baseline; lower H mound, p/q marine surfaces, curved m/n/o beneath m-prime/o-prime. No measured scale; illustrates regional subsidence and local volcanic uplift.
H is a low central swell with q at left and p at right, stippled marine beds at the flanks above baselines; this is the hypothetical littoral-deposit comparison, not quantitative data.
Grand Canary labelled section: inclined marine beds overlap older subaerial rocks, rising terrain to the right; no numerical dimensions. Supports relative stratigraphic geometry only.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
